entries.defect: PROPOSAL, adopted (enforcement of existing rules, no load added). Knob: runbook 'Acceptance discipline (kept)' — gate only the author-declared final pushed SHA, rerun only checks a later commit invalidates, stop after ONE repeat of an unchanged SHA/section/backend/failure signature and diagnose before any further run, and reuse the recorded main run for a red already charged to an open point with main unchanged in that section. Basis (inventory per-point table and Suites): 1415 ran 15 suites / 208 min with 9 same-SHA repeats and had the longest post-1444 acceptance (5.1 h); 1432 ran 19 suites with 4 same-SHA repeats; red runs are 11.5 of 15.8 finished suite hours (73 %); 1414 and 1418 each include an extra main comparison run. Expected gain: A's '1–2 h on a 1415-type point' is NOT supported — per-repeat minutes, and whether the 13 same-SHA repeats also shared section, backend and signature, are not in the material (B36), so the avoidable fraction is not measurable; the direction (fewer redundant runs) is. Risk: stopping investigation instead of repetition; treating a changed dependency or environment as 'unaffected'; misclassifying a new regression as an already-charged red. Measure over the next cycle: same-SHA repeats per point, acceptance hours per point, diagnosis-to-fix time, main-run reuses and new uncharged reds, post-merge red rate on main.

PROPOSAL, measure-first (re-tune of existing run-wait stall handling, no load added). Knob: the STALLED cut-off in run-wait ('a running/- hang is STALLED and diagnosed') tied to the suite's measured --plan duration plus a margin, plus resolving leftover run-wait/browser processes before a retry (the 23.10 B logs name a leftover run-wait.mjs process as another suite run). Basis: 5 hung 1442 WebGPU runs cost about 4.3 h (i), i.e. roughly 52 min each; a full polish-villagers run takes about 43 min per backend (median of 11 runs, 8.1 h). Expected gain: up to most of the 4.3 h whenever hangs recur; B is right that not all of it is recoverable (a hang still costs the run up to the cut-off plus diagnosis). Risk: a slow but valid run under load flagged as stalled (false red); a killed run leaving its browser alive. Measure: false-stall rate on quiet-host full WebGPU runs against the chosen cut-off (adopt only at zero), hung minutes per hang, surviving processes after a stall, subsequent suite durations and reds.

PROPOSAL, adopted as enforcement of an existing runbook rule ('Simplified': a wait declaration uses run-wait --plan, not the 45-minute default). Basis: suite durations range from a 3-min section run to about 43-min full backend runs, so a flat 45-min wait oversleeps short runs. B's link to the 35-min idle of 26.10 10:44 is NOT supported: the inventory places that idle inside 1415's acceptance without naming its cause. Expected gain: owner resumes at suite completion; not measurable from the material. Risk: more wake-ups raising bookkeeping. Measure: suite-completion-to-owner-resumption delay and wake-ups per point.

PROPOSAL, adopted as practice (the runbook already permits 'early review' during suite waits; a review is not a local heavy job). Knob: run the cross-vendor review of the next finished cloud branch while the current branch's suite runs, on that branch's final SHA. Basis (owner item a): 1418 was handed over 19:19 but reviewed only 20:56, after a 1.6 h wait while 1417's 84-min re-run filled 19:19–20:44; the resulting cloud fix was handed over 21:18 and picked up about 22:10. Expected gain: A's '1–2.5 h per queued cloud branch' overstates — 1418's suites (22:51–23:28) still needed the single acceptance lane, so the material supports at most the review wait (about 1.6 h on 1418) plus part of the 0.9 h pickup gap. Review durations are unlogged, so the net is not measurable yet. Risk: reviewing code that main's next landing supersedes (re-review); a 'remote' review path must not add local load. Measure: handover-to-review and handover-to-pickup latency per point, re-review count, and paired suite durations/reds with a review running beside them against quiet-host runs.

CANDIDATE 'two local suites at once (separate ports, memory budget)': REJECTED for now, measure before reconsidering. A and B agree no variant is adoptable from the material; the differences are which trial to run first. Decision: (1) two browser suites at once stays rejected until a same-SHA quiet/load comparison exists (durations within quiet-host spread, zero added reds, peak memory within budget) — the constraint forbids any measurable slowdown and the 23.10 cause is unproven (see U6); (2) B13's narrower trial, one CPU-only gate (build/lint/unit) beside one browser suite, is measure-first on the same protocol and is a re-tune of the 'Local heavy jobs: 1' bound, not a new mechanism; (3) B12's one local author beside one suite is measure-first and only relevant after the cloud credit expires 05.11.2026 — while credit lasts cloud authoring already hides authoring at zero local load, so it would add load for no gain. Measure for all three: suite durations and red rate on a known-green SHA under the overlap versus quiet host, peak host/process memory, and landed points/hour against a current-policy control.

FINDING plus critique of the runbook rationale. Inventory (e): the 23.10 overlap (04:59:58Z–05:10Z) comprised run A 1424 polish-children children-motion (10 min, exit 2, its red charged to 1244) and runs B 1405 polish-villagers water-stand-table at 05:02:04Z and 05:08:38Z (exit 1) plus a duplicate 05:08:27Z start that never finished; all logs warn 'MACHINE UNDER LOAD'. Only the 05:08:38 'one whole water errand timed out' check is unique to the overlap; the jar-take and pointing reds repeated on 4 solo same-SHA runs 05:14–05:30Z. Therefore the runbook's 'both overlapped suite runs of 23.10 went red' is inaccurate (run A was partial, charged elsewhere), the inventory's own cause line 'two authors' suites on one GPU' is undercut by the 1405 self-overlap and by the solo repeats, and 'load moves a suite by about a fifth' has no measurement anywhere in the material. No positive or negative concurrency setting is established; the one-heavy-job bound stays only as the conservative default pending U5's measurement.

CANDIDATE 'more cloud authors': REJECTED. Basis: every cloud branch was handed over within 0.1–1.1 h while post-1444 game acceptance took 0.75–5.1 h; after 1444 finished cloud branches waited 7.5 h behind serial local acceptance (1388 3.6, 1418 2.5, 1417 1.4) and the only measured owner idle was 35 min (26.10 10:44, inside 1415's acceptance), i.e. no acceptance starvation for a ready successor. The runbook's own condition for raising the bound (acceptance idle for want of a successor AND no finished branch waiting over a day, measured over a cycle) is not met. More authors would add waiting branches, post-sync rework risk and credit spend (expires 05.11.2026, balance unknown) without acceptance capacity to absorb them. Measure: acceptance-idle minutes attributable to 'no ready successor' and finished-branch ages over the measured cycle; reconsider only if idle is non-zero while no branch waits over a day.

PROPOSAL, adopted as practice (no bound changed). Knob: execute the existing switch-over promptly — when a local acceptance window opens and batch-in-flight --status shows no submitted/running cloud author and no finished branch waiting, commission the next ready file-disjoint queue point and declare it in the in-flight record, which must list every concurrent job because a new --waiting-on replaces the previous record; commission-guard cannot see a cloud author until it pushes a branch. Basis: authoring took 7.1 h against 33.3 h acceptance, and after 1443 a free pool commissioned nothing for want of an overlap step. Expected gain: hides authoring behind acceptance; not separable in the material. Risk: stale queue choice at a boundary, a lost declaration. Measure: submission timing relative to acceptance start, actual overlap hours, finished-branch ages (stay under one day), bookkeeping per point.

CANDIDATES 'pool and waiting branches / stale 1347' and 'is the open-branch count a good slot criterion': REJECTED as a throughput lever now. Basis (inventory d): 1347 held a slot for 45.6 h inside the window before being parked 25.10 21:38:35Z at unchanged tip e4edd697; today open=[], slotsFree=3, parkedOut=[feat/1347-garment-rebuild], so no slot is blocked; its leftover worktree (626 commits behind main) consumes no measured resource. After 1444 the binding limits were the one-cloud-author bound and serial acceptance, not POOL_CAP; the material has zero cases of a 'branches-open' refusal while acceptance stood idle. The old branches' 35–47 h waits overlap each other and the 13.4 h host-down and are not recoverable batch time; parking a finished branch does not satisfy the one-day wait limit. Replacing the bare count with acceptance capacity, host load or conflict risk would be a new criterion (new guard/router) and is barred by the freeze; the allowed action is to --park stale or abandoned branches promptly. Measure: count of commission-guard 'branches-open' refusals while acceptance is idle (zero so far).

CANDIDATE 'pulling points forward': MEASURE-FIRST, not adopted. Mechanism today (front-candidates-commission-decision.mjs): frontCandidates skips only gated and in-flight points, so a file-disjoint point beyond the first POOL_CAP (3) workable candidates is refused 'behind-front' unless an --override --reason is recorded per point — which contradicts the runbook switch-over's 'commission the next ready, file-disjoint queue point' and would raise bookkeeping. Filtering frontCandidates by the existing independentOpenPoints would be a re-tune, but independence there is only named file/directory overlap against the caller's runningFiles (unnamed and gated specs excluded; no dependency, semantic or resource independence), and the excerpt does not show what running-file set callers pass. Decisive: acceptance is the bottleneck, so a pulled-forward branch competes for the single lane and can set back front-ranked orders unless acceptance keeps strict queue order; the material has no measured case of an idle slot with a wholly colliding front. Measure: commissions refused 'behind-front' while every front candidate collided and a slot plus acceptance capacity were free; adopt the frontCandidates re-tune only if that count is non-zero.

CANDIDATE 'shorten acceptance per point: only covering suites; second backend only when isBackendSensitivePath applies': NOT ADOPTABLE from the material. Basis: 11 full polish-villagers runs took 8.1 h, median 43 min per backend, so a two-backend pair costs about 86 min before retries; but isBackendSensitivePath appears nowhere in the material, so its coverage and false-negative rate are not measurable. The both-backend picture check stays regardless. The adoptable shortening is U1 (no redundant repeats). Risk: missing backend-only suite reds. Measure for one cycle: keep running both backends and count how often the second backend is red alone on a path the predicate would call insensitive; adopt only at zero.

CANDIDATE 'acceptance steps that may move to the cloud': ADOPTED for build/lint/unit only, as already practised; browser suites, both-backend picture check and cross-vendor review stay local (cloud green never stands in for a browser suite). Basis (owner item a): 1418 ran no local pre-merge build/lint/unit, relied on two cloud gate runs (622 test files green on b5a256d and 2e90db0), ran local collision and adult-errands suites, and the mandatory post-merge land-point fast gate ran build/lint/unit (23:29→23:38). B is right that this record shows no substitution for a browser suite and that pre-merge CPU-gate execution was not uniform across points. Gain: at most the CPU-gate minutes per point, not measured. Risk: a post-merge fast-gate red landing on main. Measure: post-merge fast-gate red rate.

PROPOSAL, adopted (bug fix / re-tune of the existing autostart liveness check, not a new guard). Basis (owner item b): autostart declared the owner 'inactive (pid-reused)' at 18:09:25Z and launched f562b927 while owner 802b57ac (pid 4006293) wrote until 18:12Z; the 22-min WebGPU run on 1e681ce07 was made obsolete; cost about 0.4 h (i) plus the lost 1.1 h session context; the 84-min re-run was owed for the new SHA and is excluded. Implementation details of the check are not attached. Fix: require predecessor exit through the existing ownership fence before a pid-reuse takeover, or switch the pid-reuse path off. Gain: about 0.4 h per occurrence. Risk: slower recovery from a genuinely dead owner. Measure: takeover events against owner write evidence, recovery latency at real boundaries.

PROPOSAL, adopted as practice (author-delegate/cloud-switch dispatch). Rule: send a fix to one destination only, folding known findings into that request; picture-fix loops stay local. Basis (owner item c): the local subagent 'Fix rack eating head-scratch pose' ran 17.4 min, 70 tool uses, 181,408 tokens while the cloud session (sent 20:53) pushed 413364252/6933d7a5d at 20:56/20:59; the local push was rejected non-fast-forward. Critical-path cost measured: zero. Gain: none in landed points/hour; saves tokens and a local agent's load beside a suite. Risk: a stalled sole author delays the fix. Measure: duplicate dispatches per cycle, handover latency.

CANDIDATE 'per-point bookkeeping overhead that can be dropped': ADOPTED only as enforcement of the existing 'Simplified' rule — one bookkeeping commit per boundary for retrospective, guide-attest and queue-rank refreshes; user-order receipts keep their timing. Basis: ordinary post-landing-to-next-commission gaps were 0.15–0.5 h; the larger gaps (1440→1441 3.1 h main-based dress investigations, 1432→1333 1.3 h, 1433→1415 1.1 h, 1445→1437 1.0 h) contained investigations, so the whole gap is not removable bookkeeping, and active bookkeeping time is not separately measured. Expected gain: small, not measurable from the material. Risk: stale queue order or incomplete successor context. Measure: landing-to-next-commission time per point and bookkeeping commits per boundary.

PROPOSAL, adopted (switching off an existing mechanism). Knob: the point-427 lower-bound check in pool-cap-independent.mjs that treats POOL_CAP 3 as a TARGET while independent work is queued and demands a reason for free slots (currently satisfied per point with --slots-free '1444 bound: one cloud author'). The runbook makes 3 a ceiling only, so the demand now fires on every boundary with a free slot and produces only boilerplate. commission-guard and POOL_CAP as ceiling stay. Gain: removes one per-point justification; not separately measurable. Risk: a genuine acceptance starvation goes unflagged — covered by U7's idle measurement. Measure: free-slot explanations per point, bookkeeping time per point, ready-successor starvation minutes.

PROPOSAL, adopted as practice (refines the existing final-SHA rule). Sync main and fold known fixes into the branch before the author declares it final and before the expensive gates start; after any later change rerun only the invalidated checks. Basis: 12 syncs cost about 3.8 h (i); 1417 took two syncs (about 1.4 h); every branch that waited over a day needed post-sync rework (1414, 1432, 1333, 1297). Limits: for 1414 and 1432 the sync opened the acceptance so its cost is inseparable, and re-gating a changed SHA is required, not redundant — so not all 3.8 h is removable. Risk: postponing a necessary sync, or gating a SHA that main's next landing invalidates anyway (serial landing means the predecessor usually lands first). Measure: syncs after gate start per point, superseded suite minutes, branch age at final declaration.

FINDING (inventory Bottleneck, Suites): local acceptance is 33.3 h of phase time against 7.1 h authoring and 3.2 h landing; 85 suite runs = 28 green, 12 partial, 40 red, 5 hung; finished runs 15.8 h of which 11.5 h (73 %) are red runs. These are inferred phase estimates (commits, mtimes, session spans), not an instrumented utilisation partition, and authoring, acceptance and waiting overlap; 73 % red is not evidence that all red time was avoidable.

FINDING (inventory Window sums, runbook Measured cycle): after 1444, 9 points landed in 22.8 h (2.53 h/point), below the 3.42 h baseline as an observation, but only 4 are game points (1415 is a diagnostics dump), 1417 and 1418 overlapped, and the prescribed cycle ends only when BOTH five landed points and 48 h are reached — 22.8 h does not complete it. Attribution of the lower rate to the bounds is not measurable yet.

FINDING with critique: the binding baseline is 3.42 h per landed point (25 points, 99.0 h from the 1409 merge 21.10 19:02Z to the 1297 merge 25.10 22:05Z, minus 13.6 h host-down; 0.292 points/h). The inventory window (24.10 00:00Z to 26.10 22:29Z) is a different one: 20 points in 70.5 h = 3.52 h raw, 2.86 h without host-down. The host-down stretch has three inconsistent values: runbook 13.6 h; inventory 13.4 h = 802 min (13.37 h); the inventory's own stamps '24.10 13:54 → 25.10 02:17' span only 12.4 h (13:54 plus 802 min ends 03:16, suggesting a Z/local mix). The baseline is labelled pre-1443 although its end (1297 merge 22:05Z) lies inside 1443's drain (1443 closed 22:27Z). Any success claim must exclude host-down consistently with one figure.

FINDING (inventory per point, Bottleneck): cloud handovers took 0.1–1.1 h; post-1444 game acceptance 0.75–5.1 h; post-1444 waits total 8.2 h, all finished branches queued behind a local acceptance (1388 3.6, 1418 2.5, 1417 1.4) plus 1415's 0.6 h idle and 1451's 0.15 h — acceptance pressure, not author scarcity.

FINDING (inventory Standstill report): all 27,709 intervals carry cause 'contradictory-evidence' with journal item {previousSeq:66, seq:67}, so the whole 70.92 h sits under 'unknown' and the runbook's 'name the class that absorbed the gain' is not measurable until the journal contradiction is resolved. The evidence-type unions overlap: 'Owner lock held 70.81 h' spans the 13.4 h host-down stretch, so lock evidence is not work evidence; 17.91 h 'no work evidence' is not established idle; long main-commit gaps (16.95 h, 4.74 h) include host-down and active acceptance. A's 70.92 vs 70.5 h mismatch is explainable by the report running past the 1418 merge and is not by itself a defect.

FINDING with critique (daemon-cap.mjs, front-candidates-commission-decision.mjs, runbook Bounds): inventory (d) says DAEMON_POOL_CAP counts only running/checkpointing/stalled attempts, but activeAttemptCount counts every state outside the freeing whitelist (queued, ready-for-review, landing, landed, failed, cancelled), i.e. also unknown or corrupt states; ready-for-review frees a slot, so a daemon cap of 1 would still admit a new author while a finished branch waits, against the runbook's no-refill rule, unless handled elsewhere (not shown). A test asserts DAEMON_POOL_CAP equals POOL_CAP, and POOL_CAP also sets the depth of frontCandidates, so the runbook's 'set that cap to the bound' is not shown to be a complete valid change, and lowering POOL_CAP would narrow commissioning eligibility too. User-gated points stay blocked even when in flight or with an override. Verdict: batch-daemon stays off; daemon-on throughput under the desired bounds is not measurable.

FINDING (pool-cap-independent.mjs, openPointSpecs): the comment says a block runs to the next checkbox line, but the head regex /^- \[( |x)\] (\d+)\./ ends a block only at a column-0 numbered '- [ ]'/'- [x] N.' line, so an upper-case '[X]' or an unnumbered checkbox line is appended to the preceding point's text and inflates its file set, hence its collisions in independentOpenPoints. Relevant to U10 before any reliance on independentOpenPoints for pull-forward.

FINDING (branch-slot-decision.mjs, commission-guard-verdict.mjs): slot occupancy = unmerged local and remote feat branches minus valid parks; assigning work to a parked branch reoccupies its slot at the assignment (counted in 'adding'); a call that adds no branch is always allowed ('nothing-opened') even at a full pool; unreadable branch lists or a torn record allow commissioning fail-open with a notice, and an unreadable parked tip reads as unmoved. The guard's cap and queue decisions are therefore not unconditional, and branch occupancy is not the same quantity as running authoring processes.

FINDING (inventory Landing, Idle times): landing is about 8 min per point (post-merge fast gate dominates), 3.2 h total, never on the critical path — no case for parallel landing or dropping the gate. Idle inventory: host down 13.4 h, hung WebGPU about 4.3 h (i), owner idle ≥20 min outside host-down 47 + 54 min (24.10) and 35 min (26.10). Eliminating host downtime improves calendar throughput but not the metric, which already excludes it.

FINDING (inventory Limitations; task constraints): review durations are not logged (only review-log mtimes); local author fixes are folded into acceptance; no 1417/1418 land logs; cloud-start logs show cloud authoring also for 1415, 1388, 1416 and 1417 beyond the brief's 1433, 1451, 1418, so location comparisons must follow the logs. Exact review, repair, handover and bookkeeping savings are not measurable. Measurement protocol for every load-adding variant: real-load suite durations, memory, red rate and landed points/hour against quiet-host runs and a matched current-policy control, from existing logs and cycle notes (no new ledger fields), host-down excluded consistently, with single owner, serial landing, front-order priority and waits under one day held; the material gives no statistical threshold or sample size.

CRITIQUE (inventory Median row): 'Wait 0.6 among the 10 that waited' is wrong — the ten waits (0.15, 0.6, 1.38, 2.49, 3.6, 13.4, 35.3, 35.6, 41.8, 46.6) have median 8.5 h; the five post-1444 waits have median 1.38 h.

CRITIQUE (inventory per point): capped start→merge for 1333 (46.2 h) and 1297 (47.1 h) exceed the span from the window start 24.10 00:00Z to their merges (21:10Z → 45.2 h; 22:05Z → 46.1 h) by about 1 h, consistent with a Z start combined with a CET end — the same mix suspected in U20.

CRITIQUE (inventory Suites vs per-point rows): per-point reds sum to 38 against the claimed 40; per-point runs sum to 82, plus the two named main runs = 84 against the claimed 85. One run and two reds are unallocated; exact saved-run accounting needs reconciliation.

CRITIQUE (inventory 1417 row): 1.10 + 1.38 + 3.08 = 5.56 h (6.96 h with the 1.4 h sync) against a start→merge of 5.92 h, so the row does not sum either way. Sync is added to the phases for 1446 (0.5 + 2.87 + 0.7 = 4.07) and 1433 but contained within them for 1333 and 1297; the convention is inconsistent.

CRITIQUE (inventory items a and c): item (c) has the cloud fix requested 20:53 and pushed 20:56/20:59; item (a) has the 1418 review at 20:56 and its fix sent 20:57 with the cloud fix handover at 21:18. The 1417 row attributes (c) to 1417, yet 1417's handover cites only the 19:19–20:44 re-runs, which predate those fix commits. Which point (c) belongs to, and which SHA 1417 was gated on, cannot be resolved from the material.

CRITIQUE (inventory item d): 'held one of the three slots' understates — 1347, 1414, 1432, 1333 and 1297 were unmerged together, so the pool stood at four or more against a cap of 3 (the runbook dates the first free slot to the 1333 merge, 21:10Z, when 1297 and the not-yet-parked 1347 remained). The count-based cap was already exceeded by pre-existing branches, which is why the bare count did not bind.

CRITIQUE (inventory Window sums): '5.69 h per game point' is 22.8 h of post-1444 wall time divided by 4 game points, while those points' own start→merge times are 6.37, 1.32, 5.92 and 4.65 h; it is not a per-game-point cost, and no pre-1443 game-only baseline exists to compare it with.
